decisions.quote:
In general, the
study found no differences between men and women in risk aversion and did not replicate the original
effect of stereotype threat on risk aversion.
decisions.reason: Dependent type and original identity: The paper collects new experimental data from 321 Slovak participants to re-test the published finding of Carr & Steele (2010, Study 2a; DOI: 10.1177/0956797610384146, 'Stereotype threat affects financial decision making'), so record_type is 'replication' and the target identity in row 2431 (paired with blind target 0) is resolved and confirmed. Outcome: The authors state an explicit overall verdict in the Abstract (lines 30-32), Discussion (p. 244, lines 1078-1082), and Conclusions (p. 247, lines 1208-1211) that their study failed to replicate Carr & Steele's (2010) finding on the effect of stereotype threat on women's risk aversion (rejecting hypotheses H2 and H3 across three risk elicitation methods, including the original Porcelli & Delgado lottery task, and across implicit and explicit threat conditions). Under Step 3 Rule 1 of the codebook, this explicit overall verdict governs and establishes the outcome 'failed'.
